sources.entry: Tool Usage: Language agents in the library can use any external tools via function-calling and developers can add customized tools/APIs here.

summary.name: OpenAI function calling
summary.one_liner: OpenAI API guide explaining how to let models call external functions and tools defined by JSON schema, with code examples for Responses and Chat Completions.
use_cases: connect an LLM to your app's internal APIs
let a model look up live data such as weather
build a multi-step agent that runs tools in a loop
enforce strict JSON schema for function arguments
limit or force which tools a model calls
stream function call arguments to a UI
summary.what_it_does: The page documents OpenAI's function calling (tool calling) flow: you declare tools with JSON schemas, the model returns function_call items with arguments, your code executes them, and you send results back for a final answer. It includes worked Python examples for the Chat Completions and Responses APIs. It covers function definitions, namespaces for grouping tools, and tool search for deferring large tool sets. It also explains tool_choice options, parallel calls, strict mode requirements, and streaming of tool call deltas.
notable: Strict mode enforces JSON schema adherence, requiring additionalProperties false and all fields required
Tool search lets the model load deferred tools on demand, supported on gpt-5.4 and later
Covers custom tools that accept free-form text input and output
caveats: Tool search is only supported on gpt-5.4 and later models
Function definitions count against context limits and are billed as input tokens
Strict mode has schema limitations and fine-tuned model schemas are cached and not eligible for zero data retention
